text:
maria: Heads-up — we saw a bunch of orphan spans in honeycomb for requests that hit the API gateway then went into our async pipeline (kafka -> worker). spans start at gateway, then next span in worker has a different trace id. sampling flags also inconsistent.

kevin: ugh. are the gateways using OTEL propagators (W3C tracecontext + baggage) or some custom header?

maria: W3C traceparent + tracestate and we add baggage. gateway is nginx + envoy sidecar that injects headers. workers are python consumers using opentelemetry-auto.

samir: kafka headers can be weird — some client libs base64-encode, others drop non-ascii. we noticed header truncation for long tracestate entries. could be that.

jess: also check that the gateway isn't normalizing case or trimming `traceparent` before it reaches the producer. nginx proxy_buffer_size / proxy_buffering can mangle long headers.

kevin: quick check: what is OTEL_PROPAGATORS on the gateway and workers? if one side only has `b3` and other expects `tracecontext` you'll get mismatches.

maria: gateway: OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,baggage
workers: OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,baggage

kevin: ok good they match. so either headers lost in queue or client lib doesn't forward. can we inspect raw kafka headers on a failing message?

samir: I pulled a few messages. header present on produce side: `traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01` but consumer sees nothing. in some messages header key is `Traceparent` (capital T) — python client lowercases keys so our header consumer lookup fails.

jess: classic. solution options: 1) canonicalize header keys when producing (lowercase) 2) add a fallback `x-rw-trace` payload envelope (json/b64) with full tracecontext 3) middleware at gateway to copy trace into message body metadata.

tessa: for reliability I'd vote for (2) + (1). fallback header is explicit and survives weird broker behavior. keep it small.

kevin: agreed. propose spec:
- Always set W3C `traceparent` + `tracestate` on HTTP side.
- When enqueueing to async (kafka/sqs), add kafka header `traceparent` lowercased and also `x-rw-trace` = base64(json({"traceparent": ..., "tracestate": ..., "baggage": {...}})).
- Workers should first try standard propagator extract() on headers, then if not found, try decode `x-rw-trace` and re-inject into OTEL context.

maria: +1. also: workers should set an attribute `rw.orig_trace_id` if they have to start a new root (so we can link in traces via attributes for later join/joinset queries).

samir: note: SQS/HTTP-based queues might strip headers too. `x-rw-trace` must be URL-safe base64 and under 4k to be safe. try to keep tracestate trimmed.

jess: we'll add a small helper lib in our internal sdk: `redwood.telemetry.enqueue_with_trace(msg, topic)` that does canonicalization and fallback. will open PR.

tessa: sampling question: if gateway sampled=0 but worker sees different sampling, should we force propagate sampling decision? i think yes — gateway sampling is authoritative for that request.

kevin: agree. enforce `trace-flags` (traceparent low-order flag) propagation and if worker would normally sample but traceflags=0 then mark span as child but set `rw.override_sampling=propagated` and keep it unsampled.

maria: operational: we also should add a dashboard in console showing async trace continuity rate (percent of messages that preserve traceparent into worker) + top queue offenders.

ci-bot: Created RFC: https://redwood.internal/docs/rfcs/2026-03-span-context-handoff — includes example code snippets, OTEL env vars, and test matrix.

samir: one more gotcha — some language OT libs don't decode tracestate with commas in values. recommend we keep tracestate entries short and move large bits into baggage only if necessary.

jess: action items I will do: 1) SDK helper PR 2) gateway nginx template change to lowercase headers when adding to kafka 3) tests for kafka header pass-through.

maria: I'll own the console dashboard spec and the alert (drop rate > 2% for 5m).

kevin: i'll update the sampling policy doc and add the `rw.orig_trace_id` convention.

tessa: sounds good — thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — catching these early will save hours in debug. :relieved:
